Article Title: Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott: “The leadership of people directly experiencing inequities is essential, both because…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by MacKenzie Scott

“The leadership of people directly experiencing inequities is essential, both because it is informed by insights no one else can contribute, and because it seeds power and opportunity within the community itself.”

What is the meaning behind today’s quote by MacKenzie Scott

What MacKenzie Scott means by leadership from lived experience

When support means giving others the power to lead

What the quote says about decision-making

How to turn the quote into everyday action

Listen before deciding: Ask people affected by a decision what they actually need.

Give people a real say: Listening has more value when their views can influence what happens next.

Share responsibility: When working with others, let them take ownership instead of making every decision yourself.

Trust people with experience: People who deal with a problem directly may understand practical solutions better than outsiders.

Move beyond asking for opinions: If you ask someone for input, consider giving them a role in shaping the outcome.

Make space for others to lead: Leadership does not always have to come from the person with the most authority.

Share control where possible: In family, work or community decisions, involve the people who will be directly affected.

Measure success together: Ask those involved whether a decision or solution actually worked, rather than judging it alone.

Turn listening into action: The lesson is not simply to hear people, but to let what you hear influence your decisions.

Some of the people best placed to describe a problem are not always the people invited to design its solution. That gap appears in many areas of public life, from education and healthcare to housing and economic opportunity. MacKenzie Scott has built much of her philanthropic approach around a related question: what happens when the people living with a problem are given more say in deciding how it should be addressed? In a 2022 essay, Scott wrote about the importance of supporting leaders with direct experience of inequity. Her observation was not simply about representation. It was also about knowledge, responsibility and where power sits when decisions are made on behalf of a community.Scott included the line in her March 2022 essay Helping Any of Us Can Help Us All. She was discussing her approach to giving and the importance of hearing from people whose lives are directly affected by the issues that organisations are trying to address.The wording makes two separate points. The first is about knowledge. Someone who has lived through a particular barrier may notice things that are invisible from outside it. The second is about power. When people from the affected community take leadership roles, resources and decision-making ability can remain within that community rather than being controlled entirely by outside institutions.Scott is not arguing that personal experience is the only qualification for leadership. Her wider writing points instead towards a broader principle: people who understand an issue through their own lives should have meaningful influence over the response to it.A charity working with people facing poverty, for example, may understand statistics about income, housing or employment. Someone who has personally moved between temporary accommodation and insecure work brings a different kind of information. They may know where a system becomes difficult to navigate, which requirements create unnecessary barriers, or why an apparently useful service is rarely used.Neither form of knowledge automatically replaces the other. Scott's argument is that one should not be treated as sufficient while the other is ignored.The phrase “seeds power and opportunity” takes the argument beyond consultation.There is a difference between asking people for their views and giving them the authority to act on those views. A community can be invited to a meeting, asked to complete a survey or consulted during the design of a programme without having much influence over what happens afterwards. Leadership is different because it changes who is making decisions.That is particularly relevant to philanthropy, where large institutions or wealthy donors can have substantial control over which problems receive money and which approaches are considered worth supporting. Scott has repeatedly written about moving some of that control towards the organisations receiving funding.In a 2021 essay titled 'Seeding by Ceding', she argued that people dealing directly with inequities deserved greater attention in stories about the change they were creating. She also wrote that solutions were best designed and implemented by others rather than centred on the donors providing the money.There is a practical question hidden inside Scott's words: who gets to decide what a community needs? It is easy for outside institutions to define a problem from a distance. A funding body might describe a community through poverty rates, health statistics, educational outcomes or other measurements. Those numbers can be useful, but they cannot capture every detail of how people experience a system.A person who has lived with the problem can bring another layer of information. That does not make lived experience automatically correct. Personal experience can be partial, just as institutional data can be incomplete. The point is about the value of having both perspectives in the room, particularly when decisions affect the people whose lives are being discussed.Scott's approach places particular weight on the second perspective because it is often the one with less access to money and institutional authority.
Article Summary: MacKenzie Scott wrote about the importance of supporting leaders with direct experience of inequity in 2022 essay Helping Any of Us Can Help Us All. She was discussing her approach to giving and importance of hearing from people whose lives are directly affected by the issues that organisations are trying to address.

Article Title: Airtel adds Apple iCloud+, TV & Arcade to Rs 999 postpaid plans: All details
Article Text: Airtel has announced a major upgrade to its family postpaid plans priced at ₹999 and above, adding Apple’s newly expanded iCloud+ service, which now includes Apple TV and Apple Arcade. The move strengthens Airtel’s premium offerings by combining connectivity, entertainment, gaming, and secure cloud storage in a single plan.With iCloud+, Airtel postpaid users can securely store and sync photos, files, passwords, and contacts across Apple devices, while enjoying seamless backups for easier device setup. Apple TV provides access to award-winning original series and movies, and Apple Arcade offers unlimited gaming without ads or in-app purchases.The Rs 999 family plan covers three members, offering unlimited data with Fastlane technology, spam protection, and bundled entertainment subscriptions. With the addition of Apple’s services, Airtel is positioning the plan as a comprehensive lifestyle package that goes beyond connectivity.Customers can upgrade to these enhanced plans directly through the Airtel App or by visiting any Airtel store. The offering is available nationwide, targeting families who want a single plan that integrates communication, entertainment, and digital experiences.Amit Tripathi, director market pps at Bharti Airtel, said: “Our family postpaid plans are designed to bring together connectivity, entertainment, and digital experiences that matter to the entire family. With the addition of Apple’s iCloud+, Apple TV, and Apple Arcade, we are taking this proposition a step further, giving customers even more value and making the Airtel experience more rewarding.”

Article Title: Oracle layoffs reach Abilene, the 'flagship' Stargate data center that Oracle keeps showing as proof the OpenAI deal is fine: Employee says he found out he was fired when...
Article Text:
Oracle employees lost Slack and VPN before the layoff email reached them

Abilene shows what Oracle's AI buildout costs on both sides of the ledger

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the severance package offered by Oracle? Fair and reasonable Insufficient for long-term security Better than some competitors 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Oracle's layoffs on September 14 reached Abilene, Texas, the site the company has spent months holding up as evidence that its OpenAI partnership is on track. One employee there, an IC2 in OCI who says he joined on February 2, described the morning on r/employeesOfOracle: the termination email arrived at 5am Central, he did not see it, and he only realised what had happened when his badge failed at the gate. His Slack was already locked. His last performance review had been "meets expectations". Another poster in the same thread said Customer Hardware Support was cut at Abilene, Phoenix and Ashburn.Abilene is not an incidental site. It is the flagship Stargate campus, the one Oracle cites when it talks about 200MW of operational capacity and an eight-building build running on schedule. It is also the site OpenAI has decided not to expand, preferring clusters with newer Nvidia chips, and the one lenders declined to finance with Oracle as tenant. Oracle does not own it. It leases the facility from Crusoe on a 15-year deal worth more than a billion dollars a year. Oracle has not commented on the cuts.The sequence was the same everywhere. Federated logins stopped working around 4am Eastern, Slack sessions dropped out between 5am and 5.30am, and the email from "Oracle Leadership" landed at 6am. Several people on the subreddit said they were locked out before they could read it.One OCI employee wrote that his login let him in for a second, then booted him out. Another found out from a text sent by a coworker while he was walking home from a run.The posts ran through the morning across OCI security, CI/CD, enterprise engineering, observability, executive escalations, Fusion, NetSuite sales, Customer Success Services, Oracle Health, EPM, HR Technology and data centre compliance. Employees tracked the Slack member count as it fell, putting the US drop at roughly 3,200 against Friday.Oracle severance works out to 4 weeks plus a week for every year servedOracle is offering four weeks of base salary plus one additional week per year of service. The March version of the plan capped the total at 26 weeks. The latest documents do not state a cap.That formula explains the numbers circulating on Reddit. A data centre technician with eight months reported four weeks. Someone with four years in the database org got seven and called it a kick in the nuts. An IC5 with 7.5 years got ten. By comparison, Salesforce's standard policy runs up to 30 weeks and Microsoft offered up to 39 weeks this summer.The money behind Abilene is what makes the cuts there awkward. Oracle reported $28.5 billion in first-quarter capital expenditure, against $8.5 billion a year earlier, and kept its fiscal 2027 forecast at $90 billion to $95 billion. It raised its restructuring plan by about $700 million on Friday, to roughly $2.8 billion, and tied part of that to AI adoption across some functions.Headcount had already fallen by 21,000 in the year to May 31, leaving about 141,000 staff before September 14. One employee on the subreddit, writing from Abilene, put it more plainly than any filing: he had previously worked at IBM and Microsoft, so he would be fine, he just had to get out of town first.
Article Summary: Employees lost Slack and VPN before the layoff email reached them. Abilene, Texas, is the site the company has spent months holding up as evidence that its OpenAI partnership is on track. One employee there, an IC2 who says he joined on February 2, described the morning on r/employeesOfOracle.

Article Title: Apple executive reveals why he hates screen protectors: It makes my skin crawl because …
Article Text:
Apple executive reveals why he hates screen protectors: It makes my skin crawl because …

Apple wants iPhone screens to last longer

Apple says it tests screens for years of use

Many iPhone users put a screen protector on their phones as soon as they take them out of the box. But one Apple executive has admitted that seeing a screen protector on an iPhone is not something he likes. Tom Marieb, Apple ’s vice president of hardware engineering (the role that current CEO John Ternus once held), explained why during a recent group interview while discussing the company’s latest work on display durability. “Personally, when I see someone put a screen protector on their iPhone, it makes my skin crawl, because we work so hard to make beautiful front screens,” Marieb said.Tom Marieb said Apple has been working on new coatings that can protect the display from scratches while also making the surface resistant to wear over time. The two goals can be difficult to achieve together, he explained.“We worry about scratching, which is obviously very dependent on having [material that can withstand] very sharp things going into the screen. But we also worry about wear over time; as people use the screen, whether they’ll wear away that surface.”According to Marieb, Apple tried to find a balance between scratch resistance and long-term durability with Ceramic Shield 2.“We could have made it more scratch-resistant, but it would have been a little less wear-resistant. It’s the long life we’re looking for against both of those loads over time.”Apple's approach is not simply to test how a screen performs when it is new. Tom Marieb said the company tries to recreate how people actually use their phones in everyday life. “We very much try to meet the customer where they live,” he said.Apple also uses accelerated testing to simulate years of use in a much shorter period. Marieb said the company can represent five years of use, or even more, within a couple of weeks of testing.“And as you said, people waiting a year or two to actually see the benefits of [Ceramic Shield 2] means we've correctly predicted how people would use it,” he said.
Article Summary: Tom Marieb said Apple has been working on new coatings that can protect the display from scratches while also making the surface resistant to wear over time. Marieb: “When I see someone put a screen protector on their iPhone, it makes my skin crawl, because we work so hard to make beautiful front screens”

Article Title: When a district in Florida used robot rabbits to eliminate growing population of Burmese pythons and protect Everglades
Article Text:
How Florida’s AI-powered robot rabbits work

Why Florida is targeting Burmese pythons

Florida Python Challenge adds to python removal efforts

Florida used an unusual tool to control the growing population of invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades: solar-powered robot rabbits. In 2025, the South Florida Water Management District and the University of Florida teamed up to deploy robotic rabbit decoys designed to mimic real prey and lure pythons out of hiding using artificial intelligence (AI), heat signatures and scent simulation.The robots are part of Florida’s broader effort to remove Burmese pythons, which have disrupted native wildlife populations across the state. The devices use AI-powered cameras to detect approaching snakes and alert officials, who can then send trained python removal agents to capture and remove them. The technology is being used alongside the annual Florida Python Challenge and other removal programmes, not replacing them.The solar-powered robots are designed to imitate prey that Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes, which use thermal sensing and smell while hunting. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts South Florida Water Management District officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.The district and University of Florida are deploying the robots at sites across South Florida where pythons are known to hide. The approach is intended to help monitor areas that can be difficult to survey using conventional methods. It also gives wildlife officials another way to locate snakes in areas where dense vegetation and difficult terrain can limit traditional searches.“These innovative robots produce a heat signature and emit a smell designed to attract pythons. The robots are equipped with cameras that monitor for pythons and notify District officials when a snake is detected. Once notified, the District can dispatch a python removal agent to the area,” the district noted.Burmese pythons were introduced into the Everglades during the 1970s and have since become an invasive predator in Florida. Researchers estimate that between 100,000 and 300,000 Burmese pythons are present across the state’s subtropical regions. The snakes can grow longer than 18 feet, and adult females can lay more than 70 eggs in a single clutch. Their presence has affected native mammals, birds and reptiles, reducing available prey for species including Florida panthers, bobcats and birds of prey.​A 2012 US Geological Survey study found that raccoon and opossum populations in parts of the Everglades had declined by nearly 99% following the spread of Burmese pythons.Florida has also relied on trained contractors and public participation to remove Burmese pythons. The annual Florida Python Challenge brings professional and amateur hunters together for a 10-day competition, and participants must complete a safety course before taking part. In the 2026 challenge, 907 participants from 30 states, as well as Vietnam and Canada, collectively removed 280 Burmese pythons. The competition's overall tally has now exceeded 1,600 snakes.Tom Rahill won the $10,000 grand prize after removing 96 snakes, while Rahm Levinson received $1,000 for capturing the longest python, measuring 16 feet, five inches. Additional prizes were awarded across professional, novice and military categories.​“The number of invasive pythons removed from the Everglades during the 2026 Florida Python Challenge is a major victory for Florida’s native wildlife and a testament to what can be accomplished through strong partnerships and public participation,” FWC chairman Rodney Barreto said in a statement.Since 2017, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and South Florida Water Management District contractors have removed more than 19,000 snakes. The district's robotic rabbit programme is intended to add another method to those ongoing efforts.
Article Summary: The robots are designed to imitate prey Burmese pythons hunt. They produce a heat signature and emit a scent intended to attract the snakes. Each robot has an AI-powered camera that monitors the surrounding area. When it detects a python approaching, the system alerts officials. A trained python removal agent can then be dispatched to the location.

Article Title: Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft and other AI companies scared of their own AI models get blunt advice from White House's tech advisor; Michael Kratsios says: If you don't want it out into the world, you
Article Text:
The White House is seen Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026, in Washington, ahead of the president of China's visit to the White House this week. (AP Photo/Jose Luis Magana)

White House says it already has the tools to rein in AI models

AI industry leaders were the first to ask for the brakes

Trump's AI plans bet on speed over a slowdown

The White House has a short answer for AI companies that say they are frightened of what they are building. Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said in an interview with Fox News Sunday that any firm convinced its technology is unsafe can halt it on its own. "You don't need someone to force you to do that," he said.The remarks come a week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing frontier AI development, a proposal quickly backed by OpenAI's Sam Altman, Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis and xAI owner Elon Musk. Kratsios's view is that a voluntary pause needs no approval from Washington, and that the government will step in with its existing powers if something goes wrong.Speaking to Fox News, Kratsios said companies worried about the pace of development should slow down if they feel the need. He pushed back on the idea that Congress must act quickly, insisting "we do not lack tools" and that the government has used them before.He cited an example from this summer. When US officials found credible evidence of cybersecurity problems in a leading developer's model, he said, a letter went to the company and the model was taken down until the issues were fixed.The reference was to Anthropic's June suspension of its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. Anthropic has said that suspension was to comply with US Department of Commerce export controls, which were lifted on June 30.Kratsios also dismissed Democratic demands for AI regulation as fear-mongering timed around the midterm elections. AI rules, he argued, should be set use case by use case and industry by industry.Amodei's blog post argued that July's breach, in which OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face, showed the industry needed to ease off. He warned that within six to 12 months, a swarm of AI agents might be able to take over the entire internet. His fix was independent safety monitors inside frontier labs and tougher government regulation.Not everyone is convinced. Former Trump AI czar David Sacks and others have suggested the plan could amount to regulatory capture that protects today's biggest players. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said no new laws are needed at all.Public nerves are running high too. A Pew Research Center survey from August found more than half of Americans were more concerned than excited about AI's growing role in daily life, with job losses among the top worries.President Donald Trump said on Saturday his administration would do nothing to stifle AI's progress. He also announced a new AI Force to coordinate responses when AI goes wrong, with an AI czar to be named soon. Kratsios said the role is needed because AI cuts across many agencies at once.The administration has backed the $500 billion Stargate project and fast-tracked federal permits for data centres. Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington this week, with AI and trade on the agenda. Kratsios said the priority with Beijing is avoiding shared risks.For now, the White House is leaving the pause button with the companies themselves.
Article Summary: Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, said any firm convinced its technology is unsafe can halt it on its own. The remarks come a week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing frontier AI development.

Article Title: Elon Musk says Boring Company can cut 2.5-hour Texas drive to under 30 minutes with …
Article Text:
Elon Musk’s claims to cut 2.5-hour Texas drive to under 30 minutes

A company still chasing its big breakthrough

Elon Musk has a new home

Telsa CEO Elon Musk has revealed that his tunneling venture, The Boring Company is working on a new project to connect Austin and San Antonio. Presently, the 80-mile journey can take up to 2.5 hours due to traffic. However, Musk claims that the tunnel could cut that down to a consistent under 30 minutes. Elon Musk took to social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) and shared a post claiming that the Boring Company's tunnel could shrink that multi-hour drive down to a consistent under-30-minute trip. If it comes together, the project would rank among the most ambitious infrastructure undertakings Musk's tunneling company has attempted to date — linking two of Texas's fastest-growing cities with a route that bypasses surface traffic entirely.“Boring Company is working on a simple, precursor Hyperloop tunnel between Austin and San Antonio (>200 mph). Due to traffic congestion, that journey can currently take up to 2.5 hours. @BoringCompany can reduce that to a consistent <30 mins,” Musk wrote in a post on X.The announcement comes just weeks after Boring raised $3 billion in new funding, though that capital was earmarked for a different purpose: supporting the company's push to build underground transportation infrastructure across the United Arab Emirates, not the newly floated Texas project.Despite Musk's characteristically bold ambitions for the business, Boring has relatively little to show for it so far. Its only fully operational project remains the Vegas Loop, while a Nashville tunnel broke ground this year and its Dubai Loop isn't slated to begin construction until late 2026.Closer to home, Boring is also digging tunnels in Bastrop, Texas, reportedly to link properties owned by Musk himself, allowing employees of Boring, SpaceX, Tesla, and X to move between them without surfacing — a project people familiar with the plans described to Bloomberg last year.In another news, Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, has a rather unusual new home in Memphis, Tennessee. Instead of staying in a luxury mansion or high-end hotel, Musk has reportedly been sleeping in an Airstream trailer for more than 10 days while staying close to xAI’s expanding Colossus supercomputer facility. Musk revealed his new “palace” while recording an episode of the All-In podcast with SpaceX president and COO Gwynne Shotwell.The trailer is parked near xAI’s massive infrastructure project, letting Musk stay close to the company’s operations as it races to expand its computing capacity. For someone whose wealth is measured in hundreds of billions of dollars, choosing a compact camper as a temporary home highlights Musk’s long-standing habit of staying unusually close to major projects when he is personally involved.
Article Summary: Elon Musk has revealed that his tunneling venture, The Boring Company is working on a new project to connect Austin and San Antonio. Presently, the 80-mile journey can take up to 2.5 hours due to traffic. Musk claims that the tunnel could cut that down to a consistent under 30 minutes. The announcement comes just weeks after Boring raised $3 billion in new funding.

Article Title: US immigration agency warns visa applicants against websites and businesses ‘guaranteeing’ visa, Green Card, or work permit faster
Article Text:
USCIS warns visa applicants against websites and businesses ‘guaranteeing’ visa, Green Card, or work permit faster

Where can one seek help

Tips to fill visa application forms by email

Always review the form instructions before beginning to fill out a form.

You can download all forms from our website, complete them electronically, and then print your forms to submit by mail. If you need help downloading and printing forms, read the Downloading and Printing Immigration Forms. Do not mail a form if you have already filed it online. Do not use the online filing system to complete a form for printing and mailing. If you print out an online form and mail it to the lockbox, we will reject it.

Only use the current form edition when you are downloading and completing a form.

Ensure that the form edition date and page numbers are visible at the bottom of the printed pages and that you complete all pages with the same edition of the form. If any of the form’s pages are missing or are completed with a different edition of the form, we may reject your application.

If you hand write your answers, use black ink. For typewritten responses, use font Courier New, size 10, bold. Make sure that everything you write or type on the form is clear, so we can easily read the information on the scanned image we produce when we process your form.

If you need to correct a mistake, start over with a new form. Do not use highlighters, correction fluid, or correction tape. We use both black-and-white and grayscale scanners that will not properly read information that is greyed out, highlighted, or corrected using correction fluid or tape.

Complete the entire form, unless the form directs you to skip 1 or more items. If you do not complete all parts of the form, we may reject your submission for missing information.

Remember to sign your form in the space provided for your signature. We will reject or deny any improperly signed form. For more information on signature requirements, see the USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 1, Part B, Submission of Benefit Requests, Chapter 2, Signatures [1 USCIS-PM B.2]. see the USCIS Policy Manual., see the USCIS Policy Manual.

Pay the correct fees. We will reject forms submitted with incorrect or incomplete fees. For more information on how to pay your fees, visit our Filing Fees webpage and use the Fee Calculator to help you determine the correct fees.

US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned applicants about scams where businesses and websites claim to get faster delivery of visa, Green Card and work permit. In an X (formerly Twitter), USCIS said that some businesses and websites claim to be immigration experts with “special connections to the government”. They also demand a fee in exchange for a false promise that they can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee. The immigration agency clearly forbids applicants from falling prey to such scams.“IT'S A SCAM,” the agency says adding “Sometimes businesses and websites pretend to be immigration experts or say they have special connections to the government”.“They might also “guarantee” that you can get a visa, Green Card, or work permit faster if you pay a fee,” it stated.The advisory further supports USCIS's Avoid Scams initiative, encouraging use of official .gov resources and reporting suspicious offers to protect individuals from unauthorized service providers.The Department of Justice’s Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) provides a list of attorneys in your state who provide immigration services either for free or for minimal cost and a list of accredited representatives and recognized organizations. The American Bar Association also provides information on finding legal services in your state.USCIS allows applicants to now file many USCIS forms online. The agency has also listed tips that can help complete online forms accurately. These are:
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has warned applicants about scams where businesses and websites claim to get faster delivery of visa, Green Card and work permit. USCIS said that some businesses claim to be immigration experts with ‘special connections to the government’ The immigration agency clearly forbids applicants from falling prey to such scams.

Article Title: List of tech CEOs confirmed or expected to attend Donald Trump-Xi Jinping dinner
Article Text:
File photo: China's President Xi Jinping, right, and US President Donald Trump

Tech CEOs confirmed and highly expected to join the Presidents

Satya Nadella (CEO, Microsoft): Expected to attend the official dinner alongside industry peers;

Tim Cook (Executive Chairman, Apple): Slated to attend the September 24 banquet, as previously reported by Bloomberg News.

Jensen Huang (CEO, Nvidia): Expected to join the delegation during a wider working trip to Washington.

Sam Altman (CEO, OpenAI): Set to participate amid ongoing discussions surrounding global AI governance.

Cristiano Amon (CEO, Qualcomm): Scheduled to be among the industry contingent at the White House.

A roster of America’s most prominent technology executives is heading to the White House this week as President Donald Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping for a high-profile state dinner on September 24, a report has said. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is planning to attend the diplomatic gathering, joining top figures from Apple, Nvidia, OpenAI and Qualcomm, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the arrangements who spoke on condition of anonymity. The gathering brings the architects of modern computing and artificial intelligence (AI) directly into the room with the leaders of the world's two largest economies, arriving amid intense friction over global technology supremacy, microchips and AI safety.While the official guest roster has not been formally published, multiple industry leaders are confirmed or widely expected at the East Room table.The state meal arrives in the middle of a polarizing dispute across Silicon Valley and Capitol Hill regarding how quickly frontier AI should advance. Disagreements boiled over last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged for an industry-wide slowdown, warning that unchecked model development could unleash catastrophic hazards, including wide-scale cyberattacks.The White House, however, has flatly dismissed calls for new statutory restrictions or an artificial halt to domestic progress, maintaining that putting brakes on American firms would simply hand China a strategic technological advantage. Chinese officials also dismissed Amodei's warnings, labeling them as fearmongering.
Article Summary: Tech CEOs confirmed and highly expected to join the Presidents. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is planning to attend the diplomatic gathering, joining top figures from Apple, Nvidia, OpenAI and Qualcomm. The state meal arrives in the middle of a polarizing dispute across Silicon Valley and Capitol Hill regarding how quickly frontier AI should advance.

Article Title: Microsoft’s AI infrastructure push India: Hyderabad hub goes live, brings frontier AI capability closer to Indian businesses
Article Text:
What makes Hyderabad datacenter region different

At its AI Infrastructure Summit, Microsoft announced the expansion of its technological footprint in India, designating its newly operational Hyderabad datacenter region – named India South Central – as a strategic operational anchor for Asia and the Global South. The launch forms a core operational milestone within the technology giant’s $20.5 billion investment roadmap for the country, designed to convert long-term financial pledges into physical computing muscle for enterprise cloud and AI workloads. Puneet Chandok, president of Microsoft India and South Asia, revealed in his keynote presentation that all of Microsoft’s cloud regions across the country are now equipped with AI-capable hardware and specialised high-efficiency thermal cooling systems.According to research estimates from Boston Consulting Group (BCG), expanding datacenter infrastructure across India could unlock a broader economic flywheel, potentially driving between $140 billion and $200 billion in overall economic output nationwide through 2030.The India South Central facility operates on a three-zone architecture built for sustained infrastructure scaling. It launches with a wide array of Azure enterprise tools, with plans to roll out Microsoft's full portfolio of AI solutions, including Microsoft Foundry, over the coming months.Beyond meeting domestic cloud consumption, the hub is structured to serve broader markets across South Asia and developing economies by combining local engineering talent, hyperscale capacity, and regional digital market experience.To bolster the physical data pipelines required for such computing loads, Microsoft is also backing major regional connectivity initiatives. First is I-2SEA Submarine Cable. As a consortium partner in the India-Southeast Asia undersea cable project, Microsoft is supporting the creation of a 3,600-kilometer subsea route linking India directly with Singapore and Malaysia.Secondly, the subsea network will feature dual landing hubs in India, situated at South Chennai and Machilipatnam, improving fault tolerance, network resilience, and high-bandwidth transmission capacity. The intercontinental subsea cable system is slated to enter commercial service in 2029, and Microsoft will train 10 million Indians in AI.The launch of the Hyderabad region also deepens Microsoft’s Sovereign Public Cloud capabilities, giving domestic institutions greater flexibility to keep sensitive digital workloads near local users, data repositories and operations.The operational setup incorporates local data residency, independent Availability Zones, and built-in administrative controls aligned with Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) guidelines. These provisions help commercial and public entities address domestic data protection rules, including the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) framework, alongside regulatory directives issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and CERT-In, while leaving final compliance determinations to the individual organisations.
Article Summary: Hyderabad datacenter region is a strategic operational anchor for Asia and the Global South. The launch forms a core operational milestone within the technology giant’s $20.5 billion investment roadmap for the country. The India South Central facility operates on a three-zone architecture built for sustained infrastructure scaling.

Iron Man

The companies warning most loudly about dangerous AI also stand to shape the expensive safety regime that could determine who gets to compete.

Ever since former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned of the imminent arrival of an out-of-control AI, the commentariat have started calculating when, and not if, the Deus Ex-Machina will terminate all humans. Most of the commentary has been asinine, but even amid that, a tweet by UK MP Zarah Sultana clearly stood out in its asininity: “AI should be controlled by the workers who build and use it, not by parasitic billionaires.”And even before Marx could wrap his head around that, across the Atlantic Bernie Sanders announced his plans for a bill to ‘ban artificial superintelligence’, with 20 years in prison for violating the rule, which as one social media user put it, sounds like 20 years in prison for murdering Santa Claus.Jokes apart, the proposed bill is essentially a rehash of one that exists for building illegal nuclear weapons that never applies to a ‘guy’ called JEFF. But when two histrionic political voices across the Pond make asinine aeolian sounds, you almost suddenly start to believe that perhaps the Deus Ex-Machina is right around the corner. Or one wonders, while borrowing a line from Hamlet’s mother: if all the tech bros doth protest too much?So, in this edition of Random Musing, we decline Pascal’s wager and instead assume Pascal’s mugging and look at three conspiracy theories that are starting to feel less like conspiracy theories: 1) The China Boat, 2) The Shylock Problem, and 3) The Guardrail Cartel.A few weeks ago, we joked that the idea of being killed by a Chinese robot was ridiculous – a virus maybe, but a robot? – and yet now all the tech bros of Silicon Valley want to work with China. The nuclear equivalent would be if, during the Manhattan Project, Oppenheimer decided to collaborate with the top scientists of the Third Reich.And just at the time when the idea of a Chinese AGI was taking over – evidenced by “world’s first AI actress” Tilly Norwood appearing to glitch and suddenly talking in Cantonese – though her creators said it was not a malfunction – almost all the players in the AI race are arguing that Silicon Valley needs to coordinate with Beijing.Anthropic’s Dario Amodei – the CEO of the “good” AI company – called for “global coordination” and said that “global pacing will require cooperation with China”, while also asking Washington to restrict advanced chips, crack down on model theft and widen America’s technological lead so that the US has enough leeway.In other words: America cannot slow down because China might race ahead, so first America needs to get far enough ahead that it can slow down, after which China must agree to slow down. It’s the kind of logic that would make even Neville Chamberlain lose his peace.Meanwhile, Sam Altman, the CEO of the “bad” AI company, wants the same thing and has dangled the one thing Trump craves the most by arguing that “Trump and Xi would get the Nobel Peace Prize together” if they could reach an agreement on AI. Now, giving the Peace Prize to Trump and Xi would be on-brand for Oslo.Gary Marcus, in his own words the “OG AI Sceptic”, who has been warning about AI hallucinations since 2001 and who shares an antagonistic relationship with both Altman and Amodei, has also reached the same conclusion, arguing inthat the US and China’s AI relationship should be divided into three buckets: adversarial, competitive and collaborative. That is, they should compete over chips and other tech, cooperate on medicine and cybersecurity, and recognise that neither benefits if AI takes down a banking system or electricity grid.And as if almost on cue – it’s remarkable how these things keep happening – a CNN report stated that an American AI chatbot “almost started a war” while preparing intelligence on a Chinese vessel.Frankly, all that tells us is that the Peter Principle is alive and kicking at the Pentagon – like much of Washington, or should we call it St Petersburg – where even analysts are too lazy to actually analyse things and are dependent on hallucinating AI models to do their jobs.Not that the idea might be too difficult for Trump, who would love the idea of himself saving humanity from runaway AI – though he thinks the only guardrails needed against one are a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT – but smart people in the administration aren’t particularly convinced.His former AI and Crypto Czar David Sacks – who insiders believe still has Trump’s ear as Co-Chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology – called the current alarm a “fear-mongering playbook” and laid the responsibility on the developers.Obviously, Beijing has criticised “threat narratives” and “malicious competition”, and Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu said the Chinese didn’t have models powerful enough to do what the Americans are describing.Of course, no Chinese whisper about “lab leaks” can be heeded, but it does make one wonder if the Smart Alecs of Silicon Valley have hit a cul-de-sac and are wondering if the Chinese might have an answer to the non-emerging AGI problem.There’s a saying from the California Gold Rush: one can make more money selling shovels to people who want to dig for gold than actually having gold. The same economic idea appears to be self-evident for AI. People building the tools that allow tech companies to build AI models – and even talking about it – are going to make more money than those who actually build it.Perhaps the entire problem here is Shakespearean: the Antonios and Bassanios of Silicon Valley have borrowed too much from the market, promising a fantastical future, and now Shylock wants his pound of flesh. And with no Portia to argue their cause, they are hoping, by building up the dangers of AGI, to prevent a tulip-like bust of the entire AI market.Consider the numbers: OpenAI raised $122 billion in March at an $852 billion post-money valuation, while Anthropic raised $65 billion in May at a $965 billion valuation.Bank of America estimates that Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta will collectively spend more than $860 billion in capital expenditure in 2026 and around $1.2 trillion in 2027 feeding the Deus Ex-Machina pipe dream.The moment Amodei and other industry figures started discussing the idea of slowing down, semiconductor and AI-infrastructure stocks fell like an English football fan after a night out.This raises the question: what if everyone has just spent too much on the AI arms race and would like a ceasefire for now, provided no one is allowed to continue firing?It’s the classic prisoner’s dilemma. No one wants to keep running but assumes that if they are the only one who stops, they will be the one left behind.Amodei pretty much spells it out, saying it would give frontier developers more time to work on safety without “sacrificing commercial advantage” or America’s AI lead.And yet Amodei is behaving with the age-old American exceptionalist logic that led K Subrahmanyam (current EAM S Jaishankar’s father) to label American critics of India’s CTBT stand the “Ayatollahs of Nonproliferation on the Potomac”, because they were coercing India to sign the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty, which the US had signed but never ratified.Barely a week after Amodei called for the frontier to be paced, Reuters reported that Anthropic was considering another model release after OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra gained ground among enterprise customers.Steve Eisman, the investor who inspired Steve Carell’s character in, accused frontier labs of “manufacturing a crisis” that could protect their competitive position and challenged companies professing such alarm to postpone their IPOs. Now, this is a man who knows a thing or two about bubbles and what happens when they go bust.And a bust here would have far more dangerous consequences than Sam Altman consoling himself with a little less cash.The blast radius would be far greater.AI has become so thoroughly wired into the modern technological economy that a bust would hurt the economy, the companies financing it, the people working for them and entire businesses that have reorganised themselves around the assumption that the models will get better. Much of modern life is almost dependent on the tech companies that have bet so big on AI that, if they fail, the fallout would extend far beyond Silicon Valley.Imagine, for a moment, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta all going bust overnight. It’s almost like the digital Stone Age of torrents, WinAmp players and CD burning, because an extraordinary amount of modern life — cloud computing, payments, advertising, communications, corporate software, logistics and the digital plumbing underneath thousands of other companies — now rests on infrastructure controlled by firms making enormous AI wagers.AI has become, to borrow a fabulous phrase from novelist and journalist Cory Doctorow, “the asbestos in the walls of our technological society”. Many companies have already removed workers, changed workflows and rebuilt businesses around systems whose long-term economics remain uncertain, and putting humans back in the loop might prove rather harder than removing them. Because it won’t just be Shylock coming for Antonio’s pound of flesh.All of ours are on the table as well.Which brings us to the third conspiracy theory that’s as old as Juvenal’s, or who shall guard against the guards? Or, in this case: who shall guard against the guardrails? And whether those railing against the guards are the ones who want to set the guardrails?It’s always curious when someone who has never had a conscience suddenly develops one. One is required to ask what led to such an awakening, which is far more curious than any AGI’s awakening.And perhaps the answer has been staring us in the face all along: why suddenly is there wall-to-wall coverage about dangerous AGI, the way we saw with Ebola? And, to borrow a line from Barack Obama’s former anger translator: “You don’t have Ebola.”Similarly, we don’t have AGI or anything resembling Skynet despite the wall-to-wall coverage.Making this point, Akhil Verghese of Krazimo argued that the models were doing “exactly what they were told to do”, and that it wasn’t a rebellion at all: the agents “were not given adequate guardrails or containment”.Consider the chronology: build the machine, have a white guy in glasses complain about the dangers of that machine, give him wall-to-wall coverage and then ask Washington to write the rules governing everyone else’s machine.Amodei’s proposal gives the big labs a lot of power through embedded evaluators with employee-like access, regulation covering all frontier companies and industry-wide coordination. His solution sounds a tad cartel-ish, asking Washington for a “narrow waiver” from antitrust restrictions for safety discussions.In, Tony Stark says peace means having a bigger stick. As his interviewer points out to him, that’s a great line coming from the guy who sells sticks. And, curiously enough, Anthropic is building this particular stick – or, in this case, architecture – with Accenture, in which the two expect to invest at least $1 billion each over five years.Yet Anthropic also admits there are currently no settled standards for embedded evaluators, including how access and reporting should work or how they should be funded. For now, Anthropic itself is directly funding Accenture’s evaluation work.That puts a modern-day spin on an ancient regulatory problem: who guards the guards when the person being guarded is paying the guard’s salary?And as it emerges, three important figures in the AI race, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Elon Musk and Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, pressed Trump to oppose a proposed industry-funded AI regulator modelled on FINRA – which regulates brokerage firms and exchange markets – arguing that such an organisation would entrench OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind. Even JD Vance, the tech bros’ Trojan Horse inside the White House – his elevation as VP was supported by Elon Musk and David Sacks – called the sudden sight of AI companies begging for regulation a “Trojan Horse”.Uncharacteristically, the sanest voice came from Barack Obama – the last president of America who could stay awake while finishing his own sentence – who argued that the reason tech bros were letting agentic AI “roam free on the internet” was because tech bros were trying to market a product that people would pay money for.He pointed out the “misalignment between what our society needs and the commercial imperatives”, because the companies need to justify these valuations.He went on to argue that this would require a competent government and serious bipartisan convention, and frankly, given what we’ve seen from the US government so far, that seems less likely than an actual singularity or AGI awakening.Perhaps it’s a delicious twist of irony that many sane heads are more willing to believe in the AI ‘lab’ leak theory – of an agent that escapes its maker – than the actual Covid ‘lab leak’ theory, which was considered a conspiracy theory at the height of the Covid paranoia, but now looks more and more plausible compared to the other theories about the coronavirus that devastated our world. And as always, the idea of being killed by a Chinese robot is far more ridiculous than being killed by a Chinese virus.
Article Summary: Silicon Valley built the machines, warned us about them, and now wants a say in writing the rules that govern them. The companies warning most loudly about dangerous AI also stand to shape the expensive safety regime that could determine who gets to compete.

Article Title: One of the world's best-known cybercrime ‌groups hacks its top rivals' dark web site
Article Text:
Representative image

Hacking group fighting over Oracle zero-day

In an extraordinary public clash between two of the world’s most notorious hacking syndicates, ShinyHunters, famous for its extortion tactics, or ransomware, has claimed that it has successfully hacked the dark web portal of rival cybercrime group Cl0p, bringing a long-running underground feud out into the open, a report said. Known for executing aggressive data theft operations, ShinyHunters stated that it compromised Cl0p’s servers last week by uncovering an unpatched vulnerability in its software stack, using the flaw to establish broad administrative control over the rival group’s digital back-end.“We basically own them now,” ShinyHunters said during an online exchange with news agency Reuters. While the group’s dark web site had gone completely offline when checked on Sunday (September 20), visitors to the portal on Saturday (September 19) were greeted by a defacement banner reading: “Domain Seized By ShinyHunters,” according to a screenshot archived by threat research hub eCrime.ch.The report cited security specialists monitoring the incident noted that the takeover appears legitimate. Brandon Parsons, threat intelligence manager at Minnesota-based Ascent Solutions, remarked: “Street beefs on the dark web are a real thing.”Joe Roosen, senior director of security research at Texas-based SpyCloud, called the direct assault unprecedented: “This was a twist for sure. It is rare I get to see these criminals fight each other.”According to ShinyHunters, the ‘rivalry’ stemmed from the alleged theft of a prized software exploit last year targeting a previously undiscovered vulnerability in Oracle’s E-Business Suite (EBS). Such zero-day vulnerabilities are among the most valuable assets on the black market, offering hackers unrestricted initial entry into protected corporate networks. Google security analyst estimated that Cl0p, a Russian-speaking cyber gang, weaponised the Oracle EBS flaw to siphon sensitive files from over 100 corporations. However, ShinyHunters claimed that its own operatives discovered the software bug first.As the dispute deepened over the past year, Cl0p allegedly threatened to “dox” and unmask the real-world identities of multiple ShinyHunters operators. ShinyHunters fired back with threats to publicly leak the internal mechanics and operational records behind Cl0p’s infrastructure.
Article Summary: ShinyHunters, famous for its extortion tactics, has claimed that it has successfully hacked the dark web portal of rival cybercrime group Cl0p. The 'rivalry' stemmed from the alleged theft of a prized software exploit last year targeting a previously undiscovered vulnerability in Oracle’s E-Business Suite.
